x-nr-latency-ms.description: Milliseconds from edge arrival until the response headers are ready. For a streamed response this is time-to-headers, not time to the final event, so it is not a total-generation figure. Stamped at the edge on every response the gateway produces, success or failure.

x-nr-trace-id.description: The OpenTelemetry trace ID for this request, absent when no valid trace exists. A client may also SEND x-nr-trace-id (and x-nr-session-id) to correlate its own spans; the value returned here is the gateway's, which always overwrites whatever arrived.

x-nr-request-cost.description: Exact cost in USD; absent when the model is unpriced

x-nr-total-tokens.description: Total token count, including cache tokens

x-nr-cache-read-tokens.description: Provider cache-read tokens; emitted only when nonzero

x-nr-cache-write-tokens.description: Provider cache-write tokens; emitted only when nonzero

x-nr-budget-warning.description: A soft budget you configured was crossed by this request, which still served; absent otherwise. Value: <scope> soft_budget <spend>/<ceiling> — scope is org, team or user; spend is the USD already committed in the budget window before this request; ceiling is the hard budget; both to two decimals

x-nr-guardrails.description: Posture of the PRE-CALL guardrail chain for this request. ABSENT means this response makes no guardrail claim — /v1/models, the control plane, an auth refusal that never reached preflight — exactly as absence works for x-nr-limit-source. Absence is never "no guardrail applied"; that is the explicit token `none`. Published on every wire that runs a pre-call guardrail chain: the four text wires `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses`, and the modality wires `/v1/images/generations`, `/v1/audio/speech`, `/v1/audio/transcriptions`, `/v1/audio/translations`, `/v1/embeddings` and `POST /v1/videos`. It is ABSENT on the two FREE video collection routes, `GET /v1/videos/{id}` and `GET /v1/videos/{id}/content`, which resolve no chain at all — absence there is the contract, and `none` would wrongly assert that a chain was looked for.

value_semantics.none: No guardrail applied to this request. A legitimate state for a tenant who configured nothing, and the alarm for one who did.
value_semantics.monitor: A chain applied and nothing in it could have refused (warn/log trial modes only). It observed; it did not protect. Reporting this as `pass` would claim an enforcement that never existed.
value_semantics.redacted: An enforcing chain REWROTE part of the prompt before it reached the provider — PII or keyword redaction — and the request was then served (HTTP 200). The model did not see what you sent, so a response that quotes the prompt back quotes the rewritten one. Distinct from `pass` on purpose: `pass` means an enforcing chain found nothing to act on, and reporting a rewrite as `pass` hides the one case where request and prompt differ. WHAT was rewritten is deliberately withheld — see design_note.
value_semantics.pass: An enforcing chain inspected the whole request and allowed it.
value_semantics.partial: An enforcing chain ran but did not inspect the whole request. It means ONLY that some content went uninspected — never that something was acted on or rewritten, which is `redacted`. WHICH part went uninspected is deliberately withheld — see design_note. It is the ORDINARY answer on the two audio upload wires, `/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/audio/translations`, not an anomaly there: a client that alarms on `partial` will alarm on every speech-to-text request it makes.
value_semantics.blocked: An enforcing chain refused the request. The one response that proves a control ran, so it is never silent about it.
value_semantics.unavailable: An enforcing chain could not run, so the request was refused WITHOUT being judged (HTTP 503, `error.type`/`error.code` "service_unavailable"). Distinct from `blocked` on purpose: the content was never assessed, so the correct client behaviour is to RETRY, not to rewrite the prompt. A 503 that reported `blocked` sent callers to change content that nothing had objected to. This header is what separates a guardrail-capacity 503 from any other one.

x-nr-guardrails.design_note: POSTURE ONLY, BY DESIGN (Rule #29; gateway rules 00-gateway-rules.md §4f gate 9). The token is the whole payload. Policy NAME, policy ID, detector family, RULE COUNT, and — for `partial` — WHICH channel went uninspected are all deliberately withheld, and widening this header to carry any of them is a security regression, not an improvement. A rule count moves when a policy moves, so a caller watching it maps a tenant's controls without ever tripping one; naming the uninspected channel hands an evader the smuggling route. That is why `partial` is a bare token and stays one. Match the value EXACTLY and case-sensitively (GuardrailStatus::from_wire is case-sensitive on purpose): an unrecognised token is unknown, never a guess at the nearest one.

x-nr-auth-reason.description: Machine-readable reason a virtual key was refused

x-nr-response-cache.description: nRouter response-cache outcome for this request

x-nr-response-cache-age.description: Age in seconds of a response-cache hit

x-nr-compression.description: Prompt compression outcome for this request

x-nr-routing.description: Which chain entry answered: direct for the first entry, fallback:<n> for the entry n fallbacks deep. Absent on cache hits and refusals

x-nr-attempts.description: Provider calls made for this request, retries and failovers alike. Absent on cache hits and refusals

x-nr-intent.description: The top intent category evaluated by the preflight chain, if intent routing was requested

x-nr-funding-source.description: Which balance paid for this request: the plan's usage allowance or credits

x-nr-allowance-reset.description: Seconds until the tightest usage-allowance window resets

x-nr-tags.description: Custom spend tags for this request, formatted as key=value,key2=value2. Relayed to spend records in nrouter.spend_logs.

x-nr-compress.description: Prompt compression request toggle. Set 'on', 'true', '1' to enable prompt compression; 'off', 'false', '0' to disable.

x-nr-trace-id.description: Client OpenTelemetry trace ID for correlating spans across client and gateway.

x-nr-session-id.description: Client session identifier for correlating multi-turn conversation steps.

x-nr-client-language.description: Client SDK implementation language, automatically set by each official SDK.

error.code: string (OPTIONAL — absent on most refusals; model it as nullable/optional or a strict decoder will fail on a 401, 404 or 429)

error_envelope.description: A refusal body always carries `error.type` and `error.message`, and carries `error.code` only where the gateway can name one of the keys under `errors` — that table is the whole set, and it spans refusals at every status, for example a guardrail refusal at either end, a guardrail-capacity 503, the 402 budget refusals, and request-shape 400s such as `input_too_large`, `fallback_not_allowed`, `guardrail_not_found` and `invalid_request`. It is ABSENT elsewhere rather than invented, because a code outside this spec is a code no client's table contains. Classify on `code` when present, then on `type`, then on the HTTP status. Never classify on `message`: it is prose written for a person and it changes.

type_values.gateway_error: The gateway's own error type for a refusal that carries no more specific type — authentication, credits, model, rate limit. The HTTP status is the discriminator.
type_values.guardrail_blocked: A guardrail refused this request: the PROMPT was refused pre-call (HTTP 400), or an OUTPUT guardrail withheld an otherwise successful provider response (HTTP 400, or a terminal SSE error frame inside a 200 on a stream). One `type` for both ends, so a client branches once.
type_values.service_unavailable: A dependency the gateway needs was unavailable (HTTP 503), including an enforcing guardrail that could not run — `x-nr-guardrails: unavailable` distinguishes that case. NOT a content refusal: retry rather than rewriting the prompt.

error_envelope.join_key_note: Always present on every response, success or refusal. It is the only join key between a refusal shown to a user and the request record behind it, so surface it wherever an error is displayed.

guardrail_blocked.description: A guardrail denied the request (pre-call) or withheld the response (post-call)

detection.buffered: HTTP 400 AND (`error.code` == "guardrail_blocked" OR `error.type` == "guardrail_blocked" OR the message contains "guardrail"). The first two arms are the contract: both ends of the request now send that one token, as `code` and as `type`. The message arm is a COMPATIBILITY fallback and is required for any gateway older than this spec version, where a pre-call block arrived as `type` "gateway_error" with a message beginning "request blocked by a guardrail" and no `code` at all. Use it only after the first two have missed — never as a general classification rule.
detection.streaming: A stream's status line is already sent when an output guardrail decides, so the cut arrives INSIDE a 200 response as a terminal `event: error` SSE frame whose data is the same {"error":{"type":"guardrail_blocked",...}} document. A streaming client that only inspects the HTTP status will read a withheld response as a successful, empty one.
detection.not_2xx_buffered: On a buffered route a post-call block over a successful upstream response is converted to 400 before the response is built, so it never arrives as a 2xx. A 2xx that nonetheless carries an error envelope is a provider-origin document passed through unchanged, not a guardrail verdict.

model_not_found.description: Model alias absent or not visible to this key

service_unavailable.description: A required gateway dependency is unavailable. Also covers an enforcing GUARDRAIL that could not run, in which case `x-nr-guardrails: unavailable` is present: the request was refused WITHOUT being judged, so retry it rather than rewriting the prompt. Both are transient and nothing was charged.

plan_allowance_exhausted.description: The plan's usage allowance for this billing period is used up. It resets at the next billing period (see x-nr-allowance-reset).

plan_required.description: Only plan subscribers can use nrouter/auto, or the plan's usage allowance is paused pending payment. Named models are paid from credits.

input_too_large.description: The request's input exceeds the served model's context window. Refused before any provider egress, so nothing was reserved and nothing was spent. Permanent for this body: shorten the input or pick a model with a larger window.

max_output_tokens_too_large.description: The requested output ceiling (max_tokens / max_output_tokens) exceeds what the served model allows. Refused before any provider egress, so nothing was reserved and nothing was spent. Lower the ceiling; it is not clamped for you, because silently changing it changes what the request costs.

fallback_not_allowed.description: A model named in the request's nrouter_fallbacks list cannot be used as a fallback target by this virtual key: the key cannot route it, or it is a Smart Router alias, nrouter/auto, an allowance model or a capacity-pool model, none of which are valid targets. Refused before any provider egress; nothing was reserved and nothing was spent.

guardrail_not_found.description: A guardrail id or name in the request's nrouter_guardrails list is not owned by this organization. Refused rather than ignored: a silently dropped guardrail is a request the caller believes was inspected and was not. Nothing was reserved and nothing was spent.

nrouter_prompt_variables.description: Jinja2 variables for the prompt template

nrouter_cache.description: Use nRouter's tenant-isolated response cache for buffered text requests. Set false to force provider egress; streams are never cached.

nrouter_fallbacks.description: Per-request fallback chain: up to 4 model names, tried in order when the primary cannot be served. `model` stays the primary and is never listed here. This REPLACES the organization's fallback policy for this one call and is not merged with it. A target this virtual key cannot route — and any Smart Router alias, nrouter/auto, allowance model or capacity-pool model, none of which are valid targets — is refused with 400 fallback_not_allowed before any provider egress. Text wires only (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/messages, /v1/responses).

nrouter_guardrails.description: Per-request guardrail selection: up to 8 guardrail ids or names owned by this organization. ADD-ONLY — the listed guardrails run IN ADDITION to the ones already assigned to the key, team or organization, and a request can never remove, relax or replace an assigned guardrail or the platform moderation floor. An id or name the organization does not own is refused with 400 guardrail_not_found rather than ignored, because a silently dropped guardrail is a request the caller believes was inspected and was not. Text wires only (/v1/chat/completions, /v1/completions, /v1/messages, /v1/responses).

spend_row_metadata_fields.$comment: RESPONSE surface, not a request body. These are the customer-visible keys the dashboard spend-row route (GET /api/nrouter-proxy/spend/by-key) returns inside a log row's `metadata`. Sending one as a request field is a defect: the gateway does not read them and forwards them to the provider verbatim. Derived from nrouter-app src/lib/logs/sanitize-log-metadata.ts (CUSTOMER_FACING_NROUTER_META_KEYS, the allowlist the drawer scrubs against) — re-derive, never retype. Every other nrouter_* key in that blob is gateway-internal and is stripped before a customer ever sees it. The examples gate enforces the nrouter_ namespace only; `tags` is the caller's own key, published here to document the surface, with nothing to refuse.

nrouter_cost.description: What the customer is CHARGED for the request, in USD; null when unpriced, never a zero.

nrouter_tenancy.description: The caller's own organization/team/user identity, resolved at authentication.

nrouter_modality.description: Which modality the request was billed as (text, image, audio, video, embedding).

nrouter_units.description: The unit the charge was measured in (tokens, images, characters, seconds).

nrouter_stream.description: Whether the request was served as a stream.

nrouter_withheld_by_guardrail.description: The response was blocked by a guardrail and never delivered to the caller.

nrouter_model.description: The model actually served, after alias resolution and any fallback.

nrouter_routing.description: How the request was routed, as { attempts, served_rank, fallback_used, source }. `attempts` is the number of provider calls this request made (1 when the primary answered first). `served_rank` is the 0-based position in the chain that answered, so 0 is the primary. `fallback_used` is true when the model served was not the primary. `source` names which chain was in force: the organization's fallback policy, or a per-request nrouter_fallbacks list. Pairs with nrouter_model, which names the model that answered.

nrouter_request_id.description: The id the customer quotes in support; pairs with the x-nr-request-id response header.

nrouter_response_cache.description: hit or miss for an eligible buffered text request; null when caching does not apply.

nrouter_postflight.description: Bounded after-provider outcome projection, itself behind a field-level allowlist.

tags.description: The caller's own request tags, echoed back; additive and never authoritative for tenancy.
